facts.text: ControlEnv reads the BDDL problem information and builds the robosuite task class TASK_MAPPING[problem_name] from the BDDL file
OffScreenRenderEnv forces has_renderer False and has_offscreen_renderer True before it builds the ControlEnv
ControlEnv.step passes the action straight to the robosuite environment
ControlEnv.reset calls env.reset() until it returns and retries when the environment raises RandomizationError
ControlEnv.seed delegates to env.seed(seed)
BDDLBaseDomain.seed calls np.random.seed(seed)
ControlEnv.set_init_state loads the supplied state and regenerates the observations through regenerate_obs_from_state
ControlEnv.get_sim_state returns the flattened MuJoCo simulation state
ControlEnv.close closes the robosuite environment
ControlEnv defaults to the OSC_POSE controller
ControlEnv defaults control_freq to 20 control steps per second, so one control step lasts 50 ms
ControlEnv defaults horizon to 1000
The default camera names are agentview and robot0_eye_in_hand with camera heights and widths 128
BDDLBaseDomain is the robosuite SingleArmEnv task base class
The task base imports the mujoco Python bindings
BDDLBaseDomain.step calls super().step(action) and then reports done as _check_success()
BDDLBaseDomain.reward returns 1.0 when _check_success() and 0.0 otherwise, scaled by reward_scale
BDDLBaseDomain._assert_problem_name requires the parsed problem name to equal the class name in lower case
The robosuite observation vector of LIBERO concatenates robot0_gripper_qpos, robot0_eef_pos and robot0_eef_quat
The README example constructs OffScreenRenderEnv from a BDDL file, seeds and resets it, sets an initial state, and steps a seven-element action that returns (obs, reward, done, info)
The Libero_Kitchen_Tabletop_Manipulation problem class is registered with register_problem and extends BDDLBaseDomain
The kitchen BDDL file defines the problem LIBERO_Kitchen_Tabletop_Manipulation and its language instruction
The clone pins robosuite 1.4.0 and bddl 1.0.1 as its simulation and BDDL dependencies

determinism.notes: cap.world.reset.v1 calls env.seed(seed) and then env.reset(); upstream sets numpy's global seed and draws the object placements from it, while this package's fake uses Python's random.Random, so the same seed does not produce the same trajectory on the two

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the robosuite/MuJoCo environment: it integrates a placeholder first-order end-effector and gripper motion and models no contact, friction, mass, actuator, object placement or MuJoCo state
the task predicate, the sparse task reward of bddl_base_domain.py:165-189 and the done flag from _check_success() are not modelled: the fake always returns reward 0.0 and done false

the clone's default observation also carries the agentview and robot0_eye_in_hand camera images (128 x 128 x 3 each); the fake and this driver return only the low-dimensional robot0_eef_pos, robot0_eef_quat and robot0_gripper_qpos members, and the full camera arrays are NOT COVERED
the real MuJoCo qpos/qvel layout is not modelled: the fake's get_sim_state returns nine placeholder numbers, not the flattened state of the task model
the fake's step is one control step of 50 ms (the clone's default control_freq 20); the physics substeps MuJoCo performs inside that step are not modelled
no wall-clock pacing and no rendering: realtime_factor 0, clock lockstep, and no cap.world.render.v1 binding
snapshot and restore are not offered by this driver even though the clone exposes get_sim_state, set_state and set_init_state; no snapshot capability is bound
no physical device is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware; no upstream simulator trajectory was compared with the fake
